parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes universal state facility exclusion in government buildings including airports, parks and schools, backed by criminal trespass and a documented arrest with birth-sex ward detention, plus national binary-sex document rules and entry screening that can refuse applicants for discrepancy and consider fraud/permanent ineligibility. National custody reports show birth-sex placement, hormone removal and abuse. Courts, injunctions, private-sector carve-outs and local protections mitigate, but no effective remedy removes the core exposures; minors face additional care, school and custody risks.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex order and passport policy process new passports only as M/F per sex assigned at birth; visitor screening cable directs refusal for document discrepancy and consideration of material misrepresentation/fraud and permanent ineligibility. State drivers licences/birth certificates cannot diverge from birth sex, with fraud treatment.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; permanent ineligibility is not automatic and requires four elements with limited waivers. Civil-liberties suit challenges passport policy; some executive orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger secondary screening, refusal, stranded travel, and potential fraud investigation interacting with detention and custody systems.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National custody adopted birth-sex policies including short haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Documented restroom arrestee held 24 hours in men's ward, facing up to 60 days for trespass.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Arrestee released on pretrial release and case dismissed on standing grounds; legal aid and courts exist, though statute was never substantively tested.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility refusal leading to trespass arrest can lead directly to birth-sex custody placement, the central combined-regime harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State 2023 statute bars gender-identity-congruent restrooms/changing facilities in all state/local government buildings including airports, parks, courts, schools, universities and jails, purporting to cover private schools; refusal to leave can be criminal trespass. National order also bars congruent use in federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside state statute scope; exemptions exist for emergencies and other specified purposes. No later arrest documented after the single 2025 case.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National and state bans stack across federal, state, airport and school settings, making exposure continuous and unavoidable in public travel.

care_services.exposure: State law bans gender-affirming care for minors, bars insurance coverage for adults, requires physician administration and 24-hour waiting period for surgery, and allows conscience refusals. National orders target minor care and funding.
care_services.protection: A national judge permanently blocked some care-ban provisions in June 2024, but appeal status is unresolved; private adult care may remain partially available.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing medication continuity may face denial, delay or disclosure, especially if documents and treatment questions interact with facility or custody enforcement.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-identity protections and materials, bans trans athletes, and counterterrorism strategy prioritizes groups described as radically pro-transgender. School investigations and potential prosecution of teachers for facilitating social transition are directed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity and 2020 ruling prohibits employment discrimination; marriage recognition statute protects same-sex marriage.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing is reinforced nationally, increasing police discretion and social hostility, while litigation creates uneven, changing enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors are barred from blockers, hormones and confirming surgeries, excluded from female school sports, subject to school facility bans, and state law allows custody modification based on receiving or possibly receiving gender-affirming care. Guardian may face investigation or loss of custody in resident contexts.
minors_guardians.protection: Care bans have been partly blocked in court; no documented visitor-family removal case in dossier. Litigation and advocacy remain active.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor risks school/restroom enforcement, care denial, and parental legal exposure, compounding adult facility and document risks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Advocacy organisations issued travel advisories citing hostile laws and safety risks. Analysis reports 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k/year and labels state Do Not Travel, but finds law severity does not correlate with killing rates, so this is not evidence of organized targeting without background rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State human-relations commission enforces national employment/housing/public-accommodations protections; counties/cities covering about 55% of population ban gender-identity discrimination; national hate-crime law applies.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local protections may help in covered cities but state hate-crime law omits gender identity and police are the enforcers of facility bans, limiting recourse elsewhere.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges, care-ban appeal and constitutionality of facility statute are unresolved; remedies are slow and fact-specific. Dossier does not document airport application in practice or later prosecutions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have dismissed the sole documented trespass case, enjoined some orders, and legal-aid organisations provide document guidance. Remedies exist but are inconsistent.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty itself is exposure: a visitor cannot reliably predict whether screening, facility enforcement or litigation will protect them at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal exclusion and ineffective appeal, but this case is worse: entry refusal is joined to criminal trespass, documented arrest and birth-sex detention, placing it slightly below 0.35.

Similar birth-sex custody harm and facility exclusion, but functioning courts, private-sector carve-outs and local protections distinguish it from sustained prison assault with no remedy; this case rates above 0.25.

0.55-C involves ward placement and partial care denial without criminal arrest or possible permanent immigration consequences; this combined regime has documented criminalisation and harsher custody, so materially lower.
0.65-A has brief detention but reliable release, apology and compensation under protective national law; here protections are contested and the state itself enforces exclusion, so far lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document/facility discrepancy triggering state enforcement and birth-sex custody, reinforced by national binary-sex policy and entry fraud screening. Private businesses, local ordinances, litigation and dismissal of the sole case provide partial mitigation, but they do not cancel universal public-facility exclusion, documented arrest, custody abuse reports, or heightened minor/family risks. Execution and systematic imprisonment are not documented, keeping the score above severe 0.15-0.25 tiers.
